title: The Nag Hammadi Library, Complete Coptic — Marcion Transcription (Konvicka): FIRST GPL SEAT
edition: Milan Konvicka, Marcion project: complete Coptic (Sahidic/Lycopolitan) transcription of the Nag Hammadi Library, distributed as NagHammadi.msql.bz2 (SourceForge, marcion/1.8/texts). 59 tractates, codices I-XIII, 34,623 lines. Supersedes the sparse holdings of EA-CORPORA-01/15 (Thomas + fragments) at library scale; 01/15 remains seated as the prior witness layer.
language: Coptic (Sahidic; Lycopolitan in Codex I) in Marcion ASCII scheme; Unicode normalization layer derived in-session

license.payload: GPL-2.0 (Konvicka/Marcion) — the transcription is a modern encoded editorial artifact and is NOT treated as ownerless ancient text; the manuscripts are ancient and PD. FIRST GPL-LICENSED SEAT: copyleft carried forward on the transcription layer and its derivatives (the Unicode normalization inherits GPL-2.0); seat record CC-BY-4.0.
license.transmission_stack: MANUSCRIPT WITNESS (NHC I-XIII, Coptic Museum Cairo) -> TRANSCRIPTION (Konvicka/Marcion, GPL-2.0) -> NORMALIZATION (CHA/TLL Unicode layer, 2026, GPL-2.0 inherited) -> TLL PROJECTION (traininglayerliterature.org/originals/)
license.adjacent_layers: Tianmu Good Works Library recorded as a rendered access layer over the same Konvicka source, NOT a textual authority; Linssen PDF noted and not used (contradictory license statement: 'public domain' + CC BY-NC-SA); Claremont NHA (ccdl.claremont.edu, open IIIF) recorded as the witness-image control route; Brill CGLO acknowledged as the authoritative critical edition and excluded as access-gated.

scope: All 59 tractates across codices I-XIII with per-tractate files in two layers: text/ascii-marcion/ (transcription of record, verbatim) and text/coptic/ (Unicode normalization with printed mapping and status table). Encoding decoded and verified empirically in-session.
normalization: Mapping verified by decode against known incipits; C left ambiguous (ϭ~ⲝ both attested) and passed through; rare sigla passed through; the ASCII layer is authoritative.
